findings.title: Cancelled and rejected bookings can send confirmed invitations
findings.description: The handler checks whether the booking exists and whether the caller is authorized, but never checks its status. An organizer or existing attendee can invoke this mutation for a cancelled or rejected booking. It then updates calendar attendees and sends invitations whose ICS status is hardcoded to `CONFIRMED` in the email templates, contradicting the booking’s actual state. Validate the booking status before any writes or external updates, and cover cancelled, rejected, and pending bookings with regression tests.

findings.title: Team administrators are incorrectly denied access
findings.description: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` combines the checks with `&&`, so a team administrator who is neither organizer nor attendee receives `FORBIDDEN`. In `packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts`, `isTeamAdmin` already accepts both `ADMIN` and `OWNER`, while `isTeamOwner` accepts only `OWNER`. Use `isTeamAdmin` alone, or combine the checks with `||`, and test both roles.

findings.title: Duplicate guests are not rejected at the API boundary
findings.description: `uniqueGuests` only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not deduplicate the submitted array. The server schema likewise accepts duplicate addresses. Calling the API with `["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"]` passes both entries to `createMany`, even though the dialog rejects that input. Normalize and validate uniqueness on the server, and add a direct mutation test rather than relying on client validation.

findings.title: Mixed-case addresses bypass the guest blacklist
findings.description: Configured blacklist entries are lowercased, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. For example, a blacklist containing `blocked@example.com` does not prevent adding `Blocked@example.com`. Normalize incoming addresses before blacklist and existing-attendee comparisons, and use the same normalized values when persisting and classifying new guests.

findings.title: Guest notifications ignore disabled standard-email settings
findings.description: `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee. Unlike the neighboring scheduled, rescheduled, and location-change senders, it neither accepts event-type metadata nor checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. Consequently, adding guests sends standard notifications even when those notifications are disabled for the event type. Pass metadata from the handler, apply the existing suppression helpers, and test host and attendee suppression independently.
